findings.evidence: After obtaining a prime q dividing both n_i and n_j, step 1.1 says q divides gcd(n_i,n_j)=1. The declared dependencies give the ordinary-order maximum property of gcd, which yields q<=gcd(n_i,n_j)=1, not q|gcd(n_i,n_j). This contradicts q>1 and closes the step; alternatively cite a common-divisor-divides-gcd result. The supplier is reached from this assigned consumer through thm-chinese-remainder-theorem.

Step 2.2 asserts that schoolbook division, multiplication, subtraction, and reduction each cost O(n^2) multitape transitions. Its cited cost definitions specify which transitions are charged, and the division theorem gives quotient/remainder existence; neither supplies a long-division procedure or its transition bound. Add a deterministic binary long-division algorithm and count its O(n) quotient positions with O(n) work per position, or cite a local result proving that bound.
